items.title: Recent Hacker News Highlights
items.summary:
1. DeepSeek open‑sourced its inference engine on GitHub, drawing 989 points.
2. A Science.org article titled “Demographic ‘Doomsday’ Misses the Mark” sparked discussion with 36 points.
3. Researchers noted WhatsApp help pages contained hidden AI instructions advising against recommending a regulator, earning 587 points.

items.title: Community Posts on Product Building and Marketing
items.summary:
1. A user shared a retirement‑planner ad that generated 150 clicks, a 2% CTR, but no sign‑ups.
2. A discussion asked where the line lies between providing setup help and doing the customer’s work.
3. An author built an AI‑tool ranking site without coding; five cold emails received zero replies.

items.title: Science News Site Navigation Overview
items.summary:
1. The page notes that every print subscription includes full digital access.
2. It lists major topic categories such as Health, Humans, Anthropology, Life, Animals, and Climate.
3. Links are provided for each category, allowing readers to explore specific science sections.

items.title: AP News Bot Verification Notice
items.summary:
1. Visitors encounter a security verification page protected by Cloudflare.
2. The message explains the site is checking that the user is not a bot.
3. No news content is displayed until verification is completed.

items.title: Tech
items.summary:
1. DeepSeek released its open‑source inference engine DeepInfer on GitHub.
2. A Science article titled “Demographic ‘Doomsday’ Misses the Mark” was discussed.
3. The Nordwand Mono monospace font for coders was published on GitHub.

items.title: The day, without the siren
items.summary:
1. Grain-corridor talks continued, with the weekly ship schedule still posted.
2. A city council published an election calendar and the dates held.
3. A weather office kept a flood watch and named the rivers it covers.

title: The tools got a little quieter

items.title: The tools got a little quieter
items.summary:
1. A compiler release shipped with fewer warnings and a shorter changelog.
2. A notes app added a plain export, with no account required.
3. One outage write-up named a single timeout and the fix that followed.

items.summary:

3. A billing tool crossed a modest monthly mark and skipped the announcement.

2. A battery paper described longer cycle life at room temperature.
3. A sleep study found a small gain from a fixed lights-out time.
